reasoning: Evidence shows mixed signals for 2025 global emissions. China (world's largest emitter, ~30% of global emissions) likely declined 0.3% in 2025. Climate TRACE data shows cumulative 2025 emissions up 0.50% through November compared to 2024. However, renewable energy surged significantly (+635 TWh solar/wind vs +603 TWh demand growth), suggesting power sector stagnation. Global fossil fuel emissions still rising ~1% annually. With China flat/declining but most other regions likely increasing, global emissions probably increased slightly in 2025 versus 2024, though margins are narrow. The cumulative data through November showing +0.50% increase is the most direct available evidence.
